speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have presented for a dermatological evaluation focusing on potential oncologic implications. Please describe the specific lesions you are concerned about, including their size, shape, color, and any changes you have noticed.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC). The patient presents with multiple non-healing, crusty lesions on sun-exposed or friction-prone areas (penis, finger) and a significant history of tobacco use, which are classic risk factors for SCC. Previous treatments for syphilis and eczema were ineffective, further supporting a malignant etiology.
